newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-POPE BACK TO HITTING THE BOOKS AFTER HEADING HOME WINNER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POPE BACK TO HITTING THE BOOKS AFTER HEADING HOME WINNER.

text.p: D.C. United rookie defender Eddie Pope will not have much time to celebrate scoring Sunday's winning goal in the first Major League Soccer championship game.
Pope returns Tuesday to his studies at the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill, where he is completing his degree in political science.
Pope headed in a corner kick at 3:25 of sudden-death to lift United to a 3-2 comeback victory over the Los Angeles Galaxy on Sunday.
"I didn't think I was having the best game, but it turned out great for me," Pope said. "I've had a pretty lucky year, playing in the Olympics.
"It's a dream come true to get to play in a game that is equal to the Super Bowl and World Series. Hopefully in five years, this is going to be huge."
After returning from the Olympics, Pope has been shuttling between the nation's capital and North Carolina several times a week. Pope, 22, faces three exams this week.
"I've gotten myself into a routine," Pope said. "The coaches -- Bruce Arena and Bob Bradley -- have been very supportive. I'd come in a couple of days, practice and play."
Pope received a lesson or two from Galaxy striker Eduardo Hurtado of Ecuador, who scored off a 10-yard header in the fifth minute for a 1-0 advantage.
"He's a national team player, a great player," Pope said. "He taught me a lesson. It was my fault. I lost sight of him. I was trying to redeem myself the rest of the game."
Pope got his chance in extra time, when Bolivian international midfielder Marco Etcheverry set up his third goal of the rain-drenched afternoon, hooking a corner kick into the penalty area.
Pope leaped above the Galaxy defence and headed it past Mexican goalkeeper Jorge Campos for the game-winner.
"It was incredible," Pope said. "Marco put it on my head and all I had to do was nod it in."
The goal completed a comeback that saw United scored two goals in the final 18 minutes of regulation to tie the game at 2-2 and force extra time.

"Bruce (coach Arena) told the team to have patience, that the goals were going to come," Pope said. "We had the momentum going into overtime. We knew that if we got some shots on goal, the winning goal would come for us."
